clue.text: Fellow from western side of Midlands city

indicators.note: the western side of a written word is its left-hand start, so only the opening part of the city's name is kept

parts.note: Coventry is a city in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: Someone who comes from the west of a Midlands city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from western side of' keeps the left half of COVENTRY, dropping NTRY. COVE is old British slang for a man or chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Cove is dated British slang for a man, a chap or bloke.

clue.text: Frolic in the shrub

definitions.meaning: to frolic is to skip about playfully
the Mediterranean bush whose pickled flower buds are eaten

explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a playful leap or prank, and also the bush that produces pickled capers.

clue.text: Signaller's item not at all difficult to carry

definitions.meaning: a coloured flare fired from a pistol to send a signal

definitions.text: not at all difficult to carry
definitions.meaning: weighing hardly anything, extremely easy to lift

explanation.surface: A signaller's kit that is easy to carry around.
explanation.definitionFit: A Very light is a pistol-fired signal flare, named after Edward Very, and read plainly means hardly weighing anything.

clue.text: Angry outbursts when man takes photos?

parts.note: Philip is a man's name
pics is informal shorthand for photographs

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage whenever a man snaps pictures of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Philippics, after Demosthenes' speeches against Philip of Macedon, are bitter verbal attacks or tirades.

clue.text: Criticise celebration when not given a port

parts.note: to hammer is to attack or criticise harshly

indicators.note: something not given is withheld, so the named letter is left out of the word before it

parts.note: a feast is a celebration with food

explanation.surface: Someone slams a party where nobody was handed a port to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when not given' removes A from FEAST to leave FEST. 'port' looks like the fortified wine but is a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammerfest is a seaport in the far north of Norway, one of the northernmost towns in the world.

clue.text: Part of photographer's equipment in French town

definitions.meaning: the glass element on a camera that focuses light
A town in northern France, in the Pas-de-Calais

explanation.surface: A photographer's kit item found in a town in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens is the optical element on a camera, and Lens is also a mining town in northern France.

clue.text: Quiet as Europe's wreathed in fog

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: wreathed means twisted or coiled round, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the words as written, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: All of Europe lies silent, wrapped in fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wreathed' rearranges AS EUROPE into EASOUPER, placed after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-souper is a thick yellowish fog, of the kind once common in London.

clue.text: Current business on a holiday island

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics
biz is informal shorthand for business, as in show biz

explanation.surface: A present-day firm operating on a Mediterranean resort island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Spanish Balearic island famous as a holiday destination for clubbing.

clue.text: Feeling ecstatic, I intended to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard signals that the words are spoken, so their sound gives the answer

parts.note: sent is slang for ecstatic or transported, and I intended means I meant

explanation.surface: Thrilled, someone says they meant their emotion to come across.
explanation.walkthrough: SENT I MEANT, said quickly, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is a feeling, emotion or attitude towards something.

clue.text: Spies love a parting word

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency
love means zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Secret agents say goodbye to a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciao is an Italian word of farewell, widely borrowed for goodbye.

clue.text: Old man seen going to an air terminal, doddery politician

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: doddery means shaky and unsteady, so the letters of the words before it totter into a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly man shuffles off to an airport, a politician past his best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' is a parent, not an elderly man; 'doddery' is the anagram signal working on AN AIR TERMINAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentarian is a member of a parliament, an elected politician or legislator.

clue.text: List six balls result if no winner?

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, as in a roll call
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end

explanation.surface: A cricket over of six balls, and a query about what happens when nobody wins.
explanation.walkthrough: In a lottery, prize money not won is carried forward to the next draw. Cricket's over is six deliveries bowled by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: When a lottery jackpot goes unclaimed it is carried forward to the next draw, called a rollover.

clue.text: African thus taken with another African republic

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
Mali is a republic in West Africa

explanation.surface: Someone from Africa is linked with a second African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken with' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A Somali is a person from Somalia, a country in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Part replacement of professionals' dissertation

parts.note: pros is short for professionals
a thesis is a long academic dissertation

explanation.surface: Experts write a paper on swapping out components.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosthesis is an artificial body part, such as a limb, fitted in place of a lost one.

clue.text: A character to enjoy drink

parts.note: dig is slang for enjoy or like
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: Someone who is a real character likes a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin and It is a British cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth. 'A character' is a single numeral, not an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a single numeral, one of the characters 0 to 9 used in writing numbers.

clue.text: As he thought he had to be?

definitions.text: As he thought he had to be?

parts.words: As he thought he had to be?
parts.note: alludes to the philosopher's maxim I think, therefore I am: because he thought, he had to exist

explanation.surface: A man who reasoned that he must exist because he was thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The French philosopher argued that the act of thinking proves one's own existence: cogito ergo sum.
explanation.definitionFit: René Descartes, the French philosopher, coined cogito ergo sum, linking thought to existence.

clue.text: The drain's badly stained

indicators.note: badly done means done wrongly, so the letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: the words as written, the 's here counting as a letter

explanation.surface: A drain that has been tarnished by dirty water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges THE DRAINS, the 's counting as S here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarnished means discoloured or dulled, marked by stains on its surface.

clue.text: Female I put back in warm domestic setting

parts.note: to replace something is to put it back where it was

explanation.surface: A woman returns things to their place in a cosy home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireplace is the hearth of a house, the warm centre of home life.

clue.text: Diversion set up through arcade?

definitions.meaning: what a seaside arcade of slot machines is built to provide

explanation.surface: A pastime laid on by a games arcade.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition alludes to the amusement arcade, a British seaside hall of slot machines and games.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement is a diversion or entertainment, the very thing an amusement arcade exists to offer.

clue.text: Makes exaggerated attacks, as I resist desperately

indicators.note: acting desperately means thrashing about wildly, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone lashes out in exaggerated fashion while trying hard to hold back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' rearranges AS I RESIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To satirise is to mock through ridicule and exaggeration, often in writing or performance.

clue.text: Get out of bed maybe, emerging from amorous tangle

indicators.note: emerging from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lover climbs out of bed, disentangling from a passionate embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to rouse someone and drive them out, as from bed; 'maybe' marks it as one example.

clue.text: A Mafia chief is an extremely handsome chap

parts.note: a Mafia boss is called a don

explanation.surface: A Mafia boss happens to be very good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis, the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, names any strikingly handsome young man.

clue.text: Honour, say, a Greek finalist

parts.note: the OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: Praise for a Greek who reached the final.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a distinguished British honour awarded by the monarch. The 'finalist' is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, so it finishes the list.

clue.text: Countryman whose companion was a crook?

definitions.text: Countryman whose companion was a crook?

parts.words: Countryman whose companion was a crook?
parts.note: reads as a rural man who kept company with a criminal, but the crook is the hooked staff carried by a minder of flocks

explanation.surface: A rustic fellow who hung out with a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal but is the hooked stick carried while tending sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A shepherd tends sheep in the countryside, traditionally carrying a crook.

clue.text: Col Blimp ultimately superior to fool

indicators.note: in a down entry being superior means sitting above, so this piece comes first
ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Colonel Blimp ends up thinking himself above a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp was a pompous British cartoon officer; here 'Col' is a mountain pass, not the rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is the lowest point of a ridge between two peaks, a mountain pass.

clue.text: Boring job son's in

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the word for job

parts.note: a duty is a job or task
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: The son is stuck in a tedious task.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty means dry and dull, uninteresting, as in a dusty lecture.

clue.text: Order TV, but the last's gone

indicators.note: the last letter has gone, so the closing letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: telly is British slang for television

explanation.surface: Someone orders a television, though the final one is sold out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell someone to do something is to order or instruct them.

clue.text: Play with girls in treacle well

definitions.meaning: a drama by Chekhov about the Prozorov siblings
in Alice in Wonderland the Dormouse tells of three young sisters who lived at the bottom of a treacle well

explanation.surface: A drama featuring young girls stuck down a well of syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two definitions. The second refers to the Dormouse's story at the Mad Hatter's tea party in Lewis Carroll's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov's play is about three siblings, and the Dormouse's tale also features three sisters in a treacle well.

clue.text: Study has artist's nude finally in shock

parts.note: to scan is to study closely
Dali is the Spanish surrealist painter, so his possessive gives DALIS

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: An art study featuring a painter's nude ends in outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'in' are link words; the possessive 's of artist's supplies the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To scandalise is to shock or outrage people by breaking moral standards.

clue.text: Guy to hang about

definitions.meaning: a guy is a rope used to steady a mast or tent
to linger or remain in one place

explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a supporting rope like a guy line, and to stay also means to remain or linger.
